title: Animated three-second flash toasts
summary: Shared notice and alert flash messages use the Stimulus alert controller and toast CSS: 180 ms slide/fade entry, automatic dismissal after 3000 ms, then 200 ms slide/fade exit before removal. Manual dismissal uses the same exit animation without resetting it on repeated clicks. Disconnect clears timers; Turbo before-cache removes toasts to prevent stale history restoration. Existing reduced-motion CSS minimizes animations. Inline warnings without the alert controller remain persistent.

title: Implemented shadcn Tailwind application shell and legacy adapter
summary: The shared desktop-first ERB shell uses application-owned shadcn-ui 0.0.15 button/card/badge/alert copies with attribute preservation and fluid cards. tailwindcss-rails 3.3.x delegates to pinned tailwindcss-ruby 3.4.19; Node packages only provide v3 theme plugins, not a JS bundler. Bootstrap supplies Sass grid only; legacy controls use a Tailwind-backed adapter. Link compiled tailwind.css, not Tailwind source files; disable SassC CSS compression while retaining Sass compilation. Keep responsive overrides inside the components layer and scope legacy text-muted to avoid Tailwind color collisions. Docker builds run npm ci and compile assets; Compose needs an image rebuild after source changes. Sidebar has desktop collapse and grouped links, mobile modal/inert focus trapping, Escape/overlay dismissal and no-JS navigation fallback; profile is a native details disclosure. Wrapped search/list streams replace existing Turbo IDs; stock-search redirects target _top so unavailable-evidence errors display. Light (default), Grey (charcoal) and Dark palettes use semantic tokens at the same cascade layer, including native controls, demo surfaces, alerts and meters. The blocking non-module theme.js Sprockets asset runs before CSS; localStorage preferences sync across tabs, history and Turbo loads without a new JS pipeline. Grey also sets the dark class for upstream variants. The labelled selector is hidden without JS; denied storage reports failed persistence while retaining in-page selection. Emit hsl(var(...)) through Sass unquote rather than its incompatible hsl function. No new provider functions, business logic, fake global search or notification inbox.

title: Avi Flombaum shadcn Rails UI with compatible Tailwind
summary: The approved UI direction is Avi Flombaum's shadcn/ui on Rails, not an invented Avb package. Use the published shadcn-ui 0.0.15 gem with Tailwind v3, preserving server-rendered ERB, Sprockets, import maps, Turbo and Stimulus. Incrementally migrate the existing Bootstrap UI rather than introducing React or a JavaScript bundler. Generators copy application-owned code and overwrite customizations; inspect selected releases and component dependencies before running them. The published gem differs from upstream main; the upstream theme uses v3 configuration, not Tailwind v4.

title: Repository retrieval and ongoing knowledge maintenance
summary: Before each response, assess available context and reuse relevant session evidence; avoid redundant retrieval and unnecessary tool calls. Before substantial work, retrieve only missing, uncertain, or stale task-relevant facts. In a new or resumed session, do not assume memory parity: check decisions, implementation status, sources, and freshness; retrieve relevant records once if applicability is unknown and verify unresolved details. Reconcile conflicts with current code and explicit user decisions. Review staged changes against the store before every authorized commit; include affected fact, decision, implementation-status, and source updates in that same commit. Preserve IDs and actual dates, validate tests and a representative query, and leave records unchanged when no reusable facts change. Retrieval is local lexical search with no model/network call; Copilot still uses inference. Instructions guide rather than enforce this workflow. plan.md and todo.md are ignored local files; GitHub agents need the shared retrieval files committed and pushed.

title: ALVIS is Equibles' built-in AI analyst
summary: Equibles officially calls its built-in browser AI analyst ALVIS. It researches Equibles financial data and provides source citations. It is not a separate unverified vendor. Equibles describes ALVIS as informational research that never places trades. ALVIS credits are separate from REST/MCP daily request limits.

title: ALVIS browser feature is not proof of an ALVIS inference API
summary: Official ALVIS documentation describes browser chats, research workflows, and author-only PDF/Markdown exports. It directs developers using their own AI agent to Equibles MCP. A supported programmatic ALVIS chat/inference endpoint and automated export-ingestion rights have not been verified. Do not invent an endpoint or automate private browser APIs. Equibles data REST/MCP access is a separate integration surface.

title: Default read-only and opt-in elevated Kraken connections
summary: Read-only Kraken monitoring is implemented at /broker_connections but disabled by default pending encrypted runtime credentials and expiring owner-specific product/geography/terms review. Each refresh inspects documented key permissions/account/expiry before balances and optional latest 50 trades; exact feature scopes only. Current application password confirms setup/disconnect/elevation-review requests with a sensitive-action lockout. Elevation is a request only; no role or key activates trading. Execution-capable connections, paper acceptance, mandates, ALVIS integration, and live gates remain future work.

title: Trading, deposit information, withdrawals, and transfers are separate
summary: The proposed elevated mode uses necessary trading permissions, not unrestricted financial access. Optional deposit methods/address/status access is separately approved and does not authorize bank debits or wallet transfers. Withdrawals, transfers, and autonomous funding remain excluded from the current plan. No model receives broker keys or can change permissions or mandates.

title: Kraken conventional equities and xStocks are distinct products
summary: Kraken advertises conventional stock/ETF brokerage for eligible US residents; brokerage API access has not been verified. Kraken xStocks are geographically restricted tokenized equity exposure, not ownership of underlying shares, and have exchange API support. Never map an Equibles equity ticker directly to a token, crypto asset, or derivative. Verify account eligibility and exact venue instrument before pricing or execution.

title: Equibles engineering showcase with personal hobby trading
summary: The current direction is a professional portfolio analytics showcase using Rails ERB/Hotwire and Equibles, with personal hobby algorithmic trading allowed and proposed elevated per-user paper mode. The former commercial hub/community/marketplace roadmap is historical, not the current backlog. Public demo fixtures, private account data, paper state, and live state must remain distinct.

title: Implemented application is a stock watchlist
summary: Stock.new_lookup(ticker, user:) uses only that owner's approved retained Equibles evidence; missing owner/rights/evidence is unavailable. It never uses global developer credentials or makes an implicit provider request. Shared watchlist writes retain identifier metadata, not licensed prices, and are not a holdings ledger or trading engine. Public /portfolio_demo uses fictional decimal analytics without provider calls. Private Equibles evidence and Kraken monitoring remain gated off by default. A separate owner-only synthetic sandbox demonstrates fictional ledger mechanics, not broker paper/live execution. A public research-policy lab has no model or provider calls. Real Hotwire Native shells now exist with distinct build/acceptance gates; ALVIS integration and real elevated execution remain gated.

title: Owner-specific Equibles evidence, entitlements and bounded refresh
summary: Authenticated /equibles_evidence stores encrypted owner API keys and owner-scoped JSONB quote snapshots; snapshots are not Rails-encrypted attributes. Refreshes one exact quote explicitly, with CSRF, password step-up for credential mutation, HTTPS and no-store responses. Default config has no approved subscriptions/rights. Verify subscription, paid quotes, automated read, private display and caching; separate history/AI/distribution rights remain unknown. Database locking bounds UTC-daily attempts and deduplicates refreshes for 60 seconds; zero retries. Snapshots separate source/receipt time, quality/delay and entitlement metadata. Failures retain old timestamps without synthetic fallback. Retention purges on access/refresh and through ExpireEquiblesEvidenceJob on the maintenance queue, manually or from a separate five-minute scheduler. This argument-free idempotent job rechecks current approval and original deadlines under each row lock, without credentials or provider requests. Scheduling is best effort, not a wall-clock deletion guarantee. Scheduler health requires a recent successful enqueue; failures terminate explicitly for container restart. Expiry/revoked rights cannot be bypassed by old snapshots or retroactive extensions. Real worker processing after downtime and PostgreSQL/Redis recreation was verified with synthetic records, then cleaned up. Legacy stock/social/search price cells show Unavailable even for existing stored prices; only owner evidence may display permitted quotes. No credentialed subscription exercise was performed.

title: Private connection ownership, encryption, and read-only lifecycle
summary: Private Kraken connections belong only to their authenticated owner, use encrypted credentials/evidence, HTTPS except local development, password-confirmed sensitive actions and no secret redisplay. A unique dedicated-key fingerprint plus database row locking coordinates nonce generation, bounded refresh and disconnect. Disconnect removes credentials/evidence; unsafe scopes or revocation disable syncing. Receipts never substitute for source time. This read-only adapter has no execution, funding, generic proxy, export, job or stream path, and never supplies private data to social/public screens.

title: Synthetic portfolio provenance and explainability
summary: Public /portfolio_demo shows fictional USD inputs, per-holding source timestamps, decimal values/cost bases/unrealized gain-loss, allocation and strict concentration rules. Missing prices leave totals incomplete, missing costs leave gain-loss unavailable, zero allocation is undefined. Loading/provider-error scenarios are simulations with no provider call or fallback success. Accessible architecture/request-flow diagrams and sanitized walkthrough explain provenance/cache/failure boundaries. Sector/company/history/performance/benchmark features remain gated; this is not live research or a native-shell build.

title: Rails regression runner compatibility and watchlist authority
summary: Rails 7.1.3.4 with Minitest 6.0.6 reproduced line_filtering.rb argument-count failure. Gemfile constrains Minitest to compatible 5.27 without unrelated runtime upgrades. Initial A-E baseline passed 151 tests/2220 assertions; container foundation passed158/2278. On 2026-11-05, docker compose --env-file .env.docker --profile test run --rm test passed207 tests/2742 assertions with two workers, isolated PostgreSQL and faked providers. Coverage includes watchlist/Devise authority, encrypted private boundaries, secret generation, retention scheduling, synthetic ledger concurrency/idempotency/expiry and SQL append-only protections, explicit account-closure refusal, research-policy rejection, disabled deposit contracts, native navigation metadata and retrieval. Canonical PostgreSQL16 db/structure.sql preserves ledger triggers across parallel test schema loads. Eager loading and production image build/boot also passed; boot used only an ephemeral smoke secret. Rails tests do not verify subscriptions, eligibility, broker execution, device acceptance or legal approval. Native build evidence is separate.

title: Isolated Docker Compose Rails, Sidekiq, PostgreSQL and Redis
summary: Local Compose is explicitly approved without restoring the historical ecosystem roadmap. Digest-pinned PostgreSQL 16.15 and Redis 7.4.12 use named volumes; only Rails port 3000 is published on loopback. Existing host services/data are untouched. Separate preparation and test services use isolated development/test databases. Active Job uses Sidekiq; tests use the test adapter. Sidekiq 8.0.10/connection_pool 2.5/JSON 2 preserve Ruby 3.3.0/Rails 7.1 compatibility; Linux platforms and frozen bundles prevent runtime lock changes. Worker and five-minute retention scheduler have actual heartbeat checks. Redis uses noeviction and AOF everysec; at-least-once jobs and potential recent-write loss are not exactly-once execution/outbox guarantees. No trading jobs or Sidekiq Web UI. SQL schema persistence and official signed PGDG PostgreSQL16 client tools preserve append-only sandbox triggers across schema loads; Ruby schema cannot. Explicit LOCAL_COMPOSE_HTTP=1 permits development HTTP only for exact loopback/emulator hosts under loopback publication, never production or arbitrary LAN hosts; no forwarded-header trust. bin/compose-env exclusively generates ignored mode-0600 secrets; preserve original secrets with volumes and never use down -v as routine cleanup. Container health, isolated regressions, volume recreation, worker restart, eager loading and production image build were verified. This is local development, not production release approval.

title: Mobile means Hotwire Native iOS and Android applications
summary: Mobile means real Hotwire Native iOS and Android shells sharing Rails HTML and platform-native navigation, not merely responsive web or React Native. Native projects now exist: iOS HotwireNative1.3.1 built with Xcode26.5/Swift6.3.2; four URL tests,16 bundled-configuration cases and an isolated simulator fixture-navigation smoke passed. A separate real-Rails anonymous protected-redirect/public-research smoke passed. Signed-in follow-up stopped after two UI-test selector/focus failures; no successful signup/sign-in/sign-out/session continuity was established. Android Hotwire1.4.0 project/wrapper exists but build is blocked by missing JDK/Android SDK. Public versioned ios_v1/android_v1 configurations are navigation metadata, not authority; Android modal URI is hotwire://fragment/web/modal/sheet. Local iOS uses127.0.0.1:3000 and Android emulator10.0.2.2:3000; clients reject invalid/cross-origin/non-loopback development navigation. Private-session/recovery/device acceptance and distribution remain gates; no phone execution, bridges, public tunnel or broker-key relay.

title: Owner-only synthetic strategy mechanics are not broker paper execution
summary: Authenticated /sandbox_accounts persists a separate fictional USD ledger, bounded expiring password-approved mandates and fixed declarative trend-v1 rise/fall/flat fixtures. No provider/model input, external requests, broker key, deposits, reset, shorting or leverage. Opening cash/capital are positive up to10000, quantity1-100; notional/exposure/loss limits are required and bounded by capital, expiry within24h. Fixtures last15min in the simulation. Adverse slippage0.1% and fee0.1% rounded upward to cents; account locks serialize fee-inclusive limits/reservations/fills/revocation. Owner-bound UUID retries return original results rather than duplicate fills. Draft/active/paused/revoked transitions and expiry deny unauthorized evaluations; pause/revoke do not liquidate. SQL triggers plus ORM protections make orders/events append-only; canonical db/structure.sql is required. Account deletion is explicitly blocked for sandbox owners pending reviewed retention/closure, and enrollment warns users. These are synthetic mechanics, not licensed backtests, real broker paper fills, US-listed instruments, performance or live execution. Durable real-broker outbox/reconciliation, partial fills, ambiguous submits, calendars, separate credentials and release approvals remain unimplemented gates.

title: Synthetic research policy lab validates untrusted cited observations
summary: Public /research_demo uses original fixtures and a deterministic baseline, not ALVIS or model inference. A bounded observe-only schema pins model/rule/policy versions, fictional instrument, citations, fixed synthetic clock, freshness and expiry. Rejects unknown fields, injected instructions/endpoints, quantities, stale/missing/mismatched evidence, model changes and exhausted budgets with explicit reasons. No uploads, private records, credential access, model tools, external inference, orders or funding. This demonstrates policy mechanics, not research quality/performance, an external consent grant, a verified ALVIS endpoint or rights to ingest exports. Real-model privacy/egress/rights, licensed inputs and prospective evaluation remain gates.

title: Optional deposit-information review remains non-actionable
summary: Authenticated /deposit_information is an independent password-confirmed owner review/status surface with no credential collection, storage, transport, queue or funding operation. Default config is off; matching expiring owner/account/product/asset/network local review cannot activate an adapter. Offline validators check exact documented operation scopes/account expiry, methods and explicit monetary fields; missing fees/minimums never become zero. Legacy DepositAddresses lacks explicit asset/network identity and a memo/tag requirement indicator, so every destination is non-actionable and no address/tag is returned for use. Funding Beta needs separate review, not assumed unsupported. Actual account permissions and a safe operational adapter remain gated; future address reads must force new:false. Monitoring keys are never promoted/reused. No bank debit, wallet transfer, withdrawal, AI funding or conventional securities funding implication.
